_comment: Single source of truth for the segment list. DESIGN.md fixes these six
lowercase strings and states the list changes only by decision of the
design lead. HubSpot routing depends on them, so they are never edited
to suit a page. tools/check.mjs reads this file and fails any page whose
chip rows, router or data-segment attributes disagree with it.
'built' marks which segments have their own landing page. 'deferred'
segments keep their chip and still capture a labelled lead, they just
have no page of their own yet.
SCOPE SET 13 Aug 2026: four pages, home first as the template.
prestige and expat deferred.
FOLDERS 13 Aug 2026: pages live under 'New Builds/', two levels below the
repository root. The 'home' segment builds into the 'buyer' folder, so its
key and its folder name differ on purpose. The key is the routing label
and never changes; the folder is only a path. Every other segment builds
into a folder named after its key.
REBUILD 17 Aug 2026: the first home buyers page was rejected by the
client, deleted (recoverable at d5251d3) and rebuilt the same day from
the Paper.Design artboard 'BUYER 1440'. For this design Paper is the
visual source of truth; the token deltas against Figma are recorded in
HANDOVER.md. The rebuilt page is the template for the other three.

segments.label: Home buyer
segments.register: Reassuring, process-forward. Lead with handover of risk and the fact that a person inspects everything. Do not lead with data.

segments.label: Investor
segments.register: Evidence-forward. Lead with independence and no developer commissions.

segments.label: Commercial
segments.register: Competent, transactional. Lead with due diligence and buy-versus-lease certainty.

segments.label: Prestige
segments.register: Restrained, fewer words, more space. Lead with access to stock that never reaches the market.

segments.label: Expat
segments.register: Practical. Lead with the remote process and current foreign buyer rules.

segments.label: Developer
segments.register: Numerical. Lead with site access and resale numbers, shortest copy of any segment.

deferredChipBehaviour.assumed: Keep prestige and expat chips in every router and chip row. They select normally and post to the same capture form, so the lead still arrives labelled in HubSpot. No page, no outbound link, no dead click.
deferredChipBehaviour.alternative: Link the two chips out to the equivalent propertybuyer.com.au pages instead. Costs the labelled lead.

segmentRanking.problem: DESIGN.md says not all six can get equal treatment or nothing ranks. Every page gives all six equal weight, which the rules call wrong.
segmentRanking.status: RESOLVED 13 Aug 2026, equal weight is deliberate
segmentRanking.decision: Do not rank. The client database was never set up to qualify leads or segment the market, so there is no evidence base to rank against. Ranking now would encode a guess as a design decision. These pages exist partly to generate that evidence: every capture point labels a lead by segment, budget band and location, and the distribution that comes back is the ranking input.
segmentRanking.consequence: The router is a measurement instrument before it is a conversion device. Revisit once there is real volume, and rank on observed demand rather than assumption.
segmentRanking.supersedes: The DESIGN.md rule that equal treatment is itself wrong. That rule assumes you know the order. Here, not knowing is the finding.

tier1Proof.problem: The rules budget three Tier 1 proof blocks per page, attributable and dated. No real examples were supplied, and the slots shipped empty.
tier1Proof.status: RESOLVED for home 18 Aug 2026 and for commercial 20 Aug 2026, six still outstanding
tier1Proof.decision: The home page slots were filled 18 Aug 2026 from the client-supplied deck "Legacy All Homebuyer (1).pdf", 80 residential purchases each carrying a purchase year and price, a 2026 valuation, client savings, equity created and a time to purchase. Every figure is copied from that deck rather than derived, and abbreviated figures on the cards are exact rather than rounded. Each of the three traces to a row in paper/proof-register.md. The page carries no proof brackets; the three that remain are footer legal links.
tier1Proof.openQuestion: Melbourne is the largest single group in the deck at 23 of 80 records and is not represented in the three, because the ladder was chosen over geographic spread. The register names the two Melbourne records that could take a slot if the client would rather show three states than three life stages.
tier1Proof.safeguard: Unfilled values stay wrapped in square brackets, so an unfilled slot renders as visibly unfilled rather than as a plausible claim. tools/check.mjs used to fail hard on any bracket in visible copy; that rule was retired 18 Aug 2026 at the client's direction, because the values arrive after the proof of concept and a permanent failure on every run was drowning out the checks that still matter. The brackets remain the safeguard, the automated stop does not.
tier1Proof.outstanding: Three real proof points still needed, for developer. Investor was filled 21 Aug 2026 from "Legacy All Investor.pdf"; see investorProofSelection and the investor section of paper/proof-register.md. The commercial three were taken 20 Aug 2026 from the Reserves table in paper/proof-register.md, sourced from "Latest Recent Purchases - Commercial.pdf": Geoff (Melbourne office, owner occupier), Jamie and Tamara (Brisbane warehouse), Stella (Sydney office, bought from overseas). Every figure is copied from that deck. A price that does not abbreviate exactly is written in full in the card body and kept out of the stat row, so no figure on a card is rounded.
tier1Proof.selection: The three chosen ladder by life stage and by price so a visitor finds themselves in one of them: first home (Shane, Brisbane, 2008), family home after three auction losses (Stephen and Veronica, Sydney, 2012), downsize (Roderick and Denise, Sydney, 2014). The middle one is the closest match in all 80 records to this segment register, which asks the page to lead with handover of risk.

proyaleCase.problem: Proyale is capitals-only, so H1 and H2 render in caps whatever case is typed, against a sentence case rule with no exceptions.
proyaleCase.decision: A font limitation, not a contradiction. The sentence case rule governs how copy is written, not how a chosen display face renders it. No text-transform anywhere, and headings stay written in sentence case so the Georgia fallback renders correctly before Proyale loads.

storyPrivacyBadge.problem: The story cards carried a "Privacy protection" badge over each photograph, from the Paper design.
storyPrivacyBadge.status: HIDDEN 18 Aug 2026 at the client's request
storyPrivacyBadge.decision: Hidden in CSS, not deleted. The markup and the base rule stay intact, so removing one declaration in assets/css/landing.css brings the badge back.
storyPrivacyBadge.note: The story photographs are the actual properties purchased, taken from the client's own published success-story decks. A street number is legible on two of the three. Hiding the badge publishes nothing the client has not already published themselves, but it is worth a look before the page takes paid traffic.

commercialBudgetBands.problem: The buyer page ships four residential budget bands. New Builds/commercial/BRIEF.md asks for commercial ranges to be confirmed before build. They were not supplied.
commercialBudgetBands.assumed: Five bands derived from the $600k to $20m commercial range stated in DESIGN.md section Segments: under-1m, 1m-3m, 3m-6m, 6m-20m, 20m-plus. Derived from a stated range rather than invented, and shipped as the visible assumption rather than blocking the page.
commercialBudgetBands.consequence: Changing these option values after launch breaks HubSpot routing the same way the segment strings do. Confirm before the page takes paid traffic.
commercialBudgetBands.note: All three commercial proof records fall in 3m-6m. That is weak evidence about the middle of the scale and none at all about either end.

prestigeBandOnCommercial.problem: The template carries a prestige band reading "A quieter way to buy, for homes valued from $2m and above". That is residential copy, and DESIGN.md puts prestige on the home page only, as one restrained band, in both section Segments and section Voice.
prestigeBandOnCommercial.decision: REMOVED from the commercial page 20 Aug 2026. No commercial claim exists in the claims register to put in its place, and writing one would be inventing a service. The prestige CHIP stays in the router, so a prestige lead still arrives labelled.
prestigeBandOnCommercial.status: DECIDED IN THE BUILD, OPEN TO OVERRULE
prestigeBandOnCommercial.consequence: The commercial page has nine sections where the buyer page has ten. This is the only structural difference between them.
prestigeBandOnCommercial.alternative: Keep the band and the rhythm it gives the page. That needs a commercial claim from the client, not from us.

commercialPhotography.problem: The commercial page was derived from the buyer template and inherited its residential photography. Four truth cards, three step cards, one service card and the three auction photos all showed houses on a page about offices and warehouses. Four alt strings said home outright.
commercialPhotography.decision: REPLACED 21 Aug 2026 from the COMMERCIAL -- v1 artboard in the Paper file 01KZW0Y27PGW3NV0QJRPXAJ9DZ. Eleven slots, being every slot on that artboard that carries real artwork. Reproducible with 'npm run import-images'; tools/import-paper-images.mjs records the Paper node id, the content addressed asset URL and the crop geometry per slot, so the crops are re-derived rather than re-eyeballed.
commercialPhotography.consequence: THE FILES ARE PREFIXED, AND THIS IS THE POINT. Both pages share one assets/img and the unprefixed names belong to the buyer page. The first attempt wrote the commercial artwork over truth-card-1.webp and the rest, which silently replaced the buyer page photography as well; caught before it left the branch. Every commercial photograph is now commercial-*.webp and the buyer files were restored byte for byte from main. Any future page does the same.
commercialPhotography.openQuestion: Three of the eleven are visibly AI generated and carry garbled text a client may read as a defect: the valuation report on truth card 3, the glass wall logo behind step 4, and the small print on the auction sign. Two more are worth a look: auction 2 is the lowest resolution of the set at 672px against a 1146px target, and auction 3 is a couple on a residential balcony on a commercial page. All five are the artwork as supplied in Paper, not a processing artefact.
commercialPhotography.note: Three slots on the artboard are still unfilled placeholder frames rather than artwork, so step 1 and service cards 1 and 3 keep the buyer photography. Paper names what they should hold: notes taken during a strategy call, the Propertybuyer buyers agents, and a buyer shaking hands with the agent after winning at auction.

commercialAwardsCount.problem: DESIGN.md section Claims resolves the award count at 53 and states it replaces 50+ everywhere, sourced to the client onboarding USP document of 6 Aug 2026. The commercial page shipped 53 in both the stat callout and the bullet beside it.
commercialAwardsCount.decision: The BULLET was changed to '50+ industry awards.' on 21 Aug 2026 at the client's direction. The stat callout above it still reads 53, because only the bullet was asked for.
commercialAwardsCount.consequence: Two numbers for one claim now sit within one screen of each other: the callout says 53, the bullet says 50+. Whichever is right, the page should not say both. DESIGN.md is also now behind the page rather than ahead of it, which inverts the usual direction and will mislead the next build.
commercialAwardsCount.alternative: Both alternatives were put to the client. The first was taken: the callout was changed to 50+ on all three pages and the DESIGN.md Claims entry was corrected, on 21 Aug 2026. Nothing here is outstanding.

commercialPurposeField.problem: The client asked whether the segment router was redundant on a commercial page, since it offers home, prestige and expat options to a commercial visitor. It is not redundant, but the question exposed a real gap. DESIGN.md section Segments says this page carries two psychographics, owner occupiers facing a lease expiry and investors chasing yield, tells the build to fork them near the top rather than average the copy, and names it the page most likely to underperform. Nothing on the page captured which one a visitor was.
commercialPurposeField.decision: ADDED 21 Aug 2026. A required two option radio pair, name "purpose", values "occupier" and "investment", legend "What is it for", placed second in step one directly under the segment router. The six chip router is untouched: it is the HubSpot routing contract per CLAUDE.md rule 3, tools/check.mjs fails any page missing a chip per rule 4, and segmentRanking records that it is a measurement instrument before it is a conversion device. It also catches misrouted paid traffic, so a visitor who lands here wanting a home still converts labelled correctly rather than bouncing.
commercialPurposeField.status: DONE, NEEDS A HUBSPOT PROPERTY BEFORE IT POSTS
commercialPurposeField.consequence: THREE THINGS. First, step one now has four inputs where DESIGN.md says never more than three. Accepted deliberately: the field is a two option tap on the same chip component as the router above it, lighter than the budget select beside it, and it is the qualification that makes this page work. Second, "purpose" is a new name on the integration surface and needs its own HubSpot property, values exactly "occupier" and "investment", or it arrives nowhere. Third, DESIGN.md section Backend Handover lists three field names and now lists neither this one nor the two the page already disagrees with; see the field name finding in New Builds/commercial/REVIEW.md.
commercialPurposeField.note: Neither option is pre-selected. Pre-checking one would bias the distribution the field exists to measure, the same reasoning as segmentRanking. Required, so the fork actually arrives. assets/js/page.js was changed to validate every required control in step one rather than only the budget select, because a required control left unset inside a hidden step blocks the step two submit with an error the browser refuses to surface. That fix is generic and covers the buyer page too, whose behaviour is unchanged and was retested.
commercialPurposeField.outstanding: The form now asks which buyer someone is; the copy still does not answer them differently. The hero names both and then says "We run the same due diligence for both", which is the averaging DESIGN.md warns about. Forking the copy is the other half of this and has not been done.

investorProofSelection.problem: The investor page could not be built while its three Tier 1 slots had no source. CLAUDE.md held both investor and developer as blocked for that reason, because empty proof slots are the one thing this build refuses to fill with plausible copy.
investorProofSelection.decision: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026 from "Legacy All Investor.pdf", 75 records across four states. The three chosen ladder by portfolio stage, matching the DESIGN.md description of the segment: Mathew, first investment, Sydney 2007; Wendy, portfolio addition, Melbourne 2024; Pui Kwan and Janis, interstate with no inspection, Brisbane 2023. Every figure is copied from the deck, purchase plus equity reconciles to the 2026 value on all three, and every abbreviation is exact so no figure had to be pushed out of a stat row. Full traces in paper/proof-register.md.
investorProofSelection.consequence: The photographs came out of the deck after all. The first attempt concluded they were unreachable because no page rasteriser is available here, which was the wrong conclusion: rasterising a page and reading an embedded image are different jobs, and in these decks the photographs are stored as JPEG streams that need no rendering at all. tools/extract-deck-images.mjs walks the page tree and writes the bytes out, and the result is reproducible byte for byte. They ship at the deck native 685x419, which is exactly what every story image already on the buyer page ships at, so this is parity rather than a compromise. Named investor-story-1 to 3 under the page prefix, so they cannot disturb the buyer or commercial photography.
investorProofSelection.note: This page gives three states where the commercial page gave one, which answers the geographic spread question raised under tier1Proof for that page. Three records remain outstanding for developer.
investorProofSelection.deckContradictsItself: Deck page 20 calls the property an apartment twice in its own copy, while the three photographs on that same page are of a freestanding cottage with a picket fence. Rather than pick a side, slot 1 names no dwelling type: the heading reads "Inner west, Sydney" and the body reads "his first investment a short walk from the light rail". Every figure is unchanged and nothing on the card can contradict the photograph beside it. Worth a client answer alongside investorDeckOverlap, because the deck is the thing that is inconsistent.

investorBudgetBands.problem: New Builds/investor/BRIEF.md needed investor ranges confirmed before build. They were not supplied, the same position the commercial page was in.
investorBudgetBands.assumed: Five bands derived from the $650k to $2m investor range stated in DESIGN.md section Segments: under-650k, 650k-1m, 1m-1.5m, 1.5m-2m, 2m-plus. Derived from a stated range rather than invented, and shipped as the visible assumption rather than blocking the page.
investorBudgetBands.consequence: Changing these option values after launch breaks HubSpot routing the same way the segment strings do. Confirm before the page takes paid traffic. The union across the three built pages is now fourteen distinct values with no overlap, which is the concrete input the HubSpot schema decision described in DESIGN.md section Backend Handover has been waiting on.
investorBudgetBands.note: The scale runs wider than the stated range at both ends on purpose, so a lead outside it still arrives labelled rather than bouncing off the dropdown. Slot 1 of the proof sits below the band at $580,000, but it was bought in 2007 and the card carries the year.

investorDeckOverlap.problem: "Legacy All Investor.pdf" retells all three of the buyer page's live Tier 1 records as investment purchases, with identical figures and near-identical sentences. Roderick and Denise are downsizers on the live page and a portfolio addition let at $4,500 pw in the deck. Rozanne is an upsizer on the page and expanding a portfolio at $1,000 pw in the deck. Shane bought his first home after years of renting on the page, and his first investment let at 5.3 percent in the deck.
investorDeckOverlap.status: RAISED 21 Aug 2026, UNRESOLVED, NEEDS THE CLIENT
investorDeckOverlap.decision: None of the three overlapping records is used on the investor page. The three selected appear only in the investor deck, so they carry no contradiction of their own.
investorDeckOverlap.consequence: The two framings are mutually exclusive: an owner-occupied home does not carry a rental yield and a weekly rent. If the investment framing is the accurate one, the three Tier 1 cards on the buyer page now in production are mis-labelled. That page sits on another branch and was not touched. And if three records were re-narrated, the other 72 in the deck cannot be assumed clean.
investorDeckOverlap.alternative: DESIGN.md places contested claims at Tier 3, which does not render. Applied strictly, that would pull the buyer page's three cards until the client confirms which framing is correct. That is a call for the design lead rather than for a build.
investorDeckOverlap.outstanding: Confirmation from the client of which framing is correct for those three, and whether any record in the investor deck also appears in the homebuyer or commercial decks under a different story.

prestigeBandOnInvestor.decision: REMOVED 21 Aug 2026, the same decision and the same reasoning as prestigeBandOnCommercial. DESIGN.md puts prestige on the home page only, in both section Segments and section Voice, and the band's copy is residential owner-occupier language with no investor equivalent in the claims register. The prestige CHIP stays in the router, so a prestige lead still arrives labelled.
prestigeBandOnInvestor.status: DECIDED IN THE BUILD, OPEN TO OVERRULE
prestigeBandOnInvestor.consequence: The investor page has nine sections where the buyer page has ten, matching the commercial page. Two of the three built pages now drop this band, so it is the home page that is the exception rather than these.

investorPhotography.problem: The investor page was derived from the buyer template and inherited its residential photography in every slot. The INVESTOR -- v1 artboard is not residential; it is the COMMERCIAL -- v1 artboard with five slots deliberately reverted to the home photography, because an investor buys both a warehouse and a unit.
investorPhotography.decision: MATCHED TO THE ARTBOARD 21 Aug 2026, six slots moved to the commercial photography and eleven left on the buyer photography. Commercial now: truth cards 1 and 3, step 2, and all three auction strip photos. Buyer kept: truth cards 2 and 4, steps 1, 3 and 4, all three service cards, the hero trio, the truth documents and the stats collage. Every slot was read off the artboard by its Paper node fill rather than by eye, and the six commercial files already existed from the commercial build, so no artwork was imported or re-cropped.
investorPhotography.consequence: One alt string changed with its picture: step 2 is now an agent inspecting shortlisted premises rather than a shortlisted home. The other five carry alt text that already described the subject rather than the property type, or are decorative. No file in assets/img was written, so neither the buyer nor the commercial page moved.
investorPhotography.openQuestion: Auction 3 is the couple on a residential balcony flagged under commercialPhotography as wrong for a commercial page. On an investor page it reads correctly, so the same photograph is a defect on one page and right on the other. The two AI artefacts flagged there also arrive here: the garbled valuation report on truth card 3 and the small print on the auction sign.
investorPhotography.retires: The investor half of buyerOffMarketPhotography. That record accepted the investor Off-market strip changing whenever the buyer strip did, because both pages referenced the same unprefixed auction files. The investor strip now points at the commercial- prefixed files its own artboard shows, so the two pages no longer move together and neither needs an investor- prefixed copy of the buyer artwork.

buyerOffMarketPhotography.decision: Replaced the three photographs in the buyer page Off-market and auction ready strip on 21 Aug 2026, from the BUYER v3 artboard in Paper, image row 8BR-0. Paper crops by oversizing a rectangle inside a smaller frame, so each visible window is a function of the rectangle size and its offset against the 573x680 frame. Those numbers are recorded in tools/import-paper-images.mjs against the asset ids they were measured from, rather than being read back off a screenshot. Two of the three reach 1146x1360; the third ships native at 906x1075 because its source has no more pixels and nothing is ever enlarged.
buyerOffMarketPhotography.status: DONE 21 Aug 2026, the investor side effect was retired the same day, see investorPhotography
buyerOffMarketPhotography.consequence: The investor page references the same unprefixed auction-1, auction-2 and auction-3 files, so its Off-market strip changed with the buyer page. Both pages carry the identical section under the identical heading, and both were already showing the same images, so the new photography suits each equally. If the investor page should hold different photography it needs its own investor- prefixed copies, which is the rule CLAUDE.md already states for every page after the buyer.
buyerOffMarketPhotography.alternative: Give the buyer page buyer- prefixed copies and leave the shared names pointing at the older images. Rejected because the unprefixed names belong to the buyer page by the stated convention, so prefixing the owner rather than the borrower would invert it.

awardsCountOnStatRow.problem: The stat row read 53 industry awards while the bullet directly below it read 50+, on all three built pages. One claim, two numbers, within a single screen.
awardsCountOnStatRow.status: DECIDED BY THE CLIENT 21 Aug 2026, DESIGN.md IS BEHIND
awardsCountOnStatRow.decision: The stat row now reads 50+ on buyer, commercial and investor. DESIGN.md section Claims resolved this the other way at the time: the landing page build brief of 6 Aug 2026 cleared 53 and stated it replaced 50+ everywhere, sourced to the client own onboarding USP document. The client asked for 50+ on the stat row, which overrules that. The bullets were already 50+ and were left as they were.
awardsCountOnStatRow.consequence: The exposure runs the safe way. 50+ understates a verified 53, so the pages now claim less than the client can evidence rather than more, and the contradiction inside the section is gone. DESIGN.md section Claims was corrected in the same pass, along with HANDOVER.md, both page BRIEFs, the commercial REVIEW, all three copy decks and the proof register, so no document now tells the next build to put 53 back. Where 53 still appears it is dated history describing the change. The hero award list names the individual wins rather than a total and is unaffected.
awardsCountOnStatRow.outstanding: The buyer page bullet reads "Over 50+ industry awards", which doubles the qualifier and is the only one of the three phrased that way. Left as found because it was outside the instruction. Commercial and investor both read "50+ industry awards."

cssLayerSplit.decision: assets/css/styles.css was split into four layers on 21 Aug 2026: tokens.css (the Figma Mapped aliases, the Paper addendum and the two faces), base.css (reset, base type, buttons, pills), landing.css (the paid segment pages) and locations.css (the location pages, empty). Every page loads tokens, then base, then exactly one design layer. styles.css was deleted rather than kept as a shim, because a path that still works is how two stylesheets drift apart.
cssLayerSplit.reason: One stylesheet serving every page means parallel branches collide in the file where a bad merge costs most. That was tolerable for four segment pages built one at a time. It stopped being tolerable when the location pages became a second page family with its own branch.
cssLayerSplit.verification: The split is comment level only. Every code line was preserved and none was added, checked by sorted line comparison, and the brace count is identical at 436. npm run check passes every rendered check at 390, 768, 1100 and 1440 on the buyer page, including the H1 and H2 token sizes and the section rhythm, so the rendered result is unchanged.
cssLayerSplit.consequence: tokens.css and base.css are shared, so a change to either lands on pages someone else may be building on another branch. Treat them the way you would treat a change to Figma Variables. A component wanted by both families gets promoted into base.css and recorded here, never copied.
cssLayerSplit.enforcement: tools/check.mjs fails a page whose first two stylesheets are not tokens.css then base.css, a page loading zero or two design layers, a raw hex in any layer, and a :root block in any layer other than tokens.css.

developerSectionCount.problem: New Builds/developer/BRIEF.md reads "expect to drop or compress one of the mid-page sections rather than pad it to match home", and treats cutting one as following the rules rather than deviating. DESIGN.md sections Segments and Voice both call for the shortest copy of any segment.
developerSectionCount.decision: NO MID-PAGE SECTION CUT, 21 Aug 2026, at the client direction. The page ships nine sections, dropping only the prestige band, which matches commercial and investor exactly. The shortest-copy rule is met inside the sections instead: all four step bodies, both changed real-access bodies and three of four truth card bodies are shorter than their buyer-page equivalents.
developerSectionCount.status: DECIDED IN THE BUILD, OPEN TO OVERRULE
developerSectionCount.consequence: All three derived pages now have the same nine sections, so the structure is uniform across the set and the home page is the only ten-section page. The cost is that "shortest copy of any segment" is now a claim about compression rather than a visible structural difference, and nothing automated measures it. tools/check.mjs does not count body copy, so a later edit could pad this page past commercial or investor without failing anything.
developerSectionCount.alternative: Cut the services band, which was the recommendation before the client site was read. It is now the weakest of the three candidates, because two of its three cards carry the client own development-specific service names.

developerClientSiteAsSource.problem: The developer page could not be honestly built from DESIGN.md alone. Three Tier 1 slots had no source, the feasibility capability was unknown and therefore ungatable, and the budget was a single open-ended number.
developerClientSiteAsSource.decision: TWO CLIENT PAGES READ 21 Aug 2026 and used as a claim source: propertybuyer.com.au/services/development-site-acquisitions and propertybuyer.com.au/who-we-help/property-developers. Treated as the client own published claims, the same footing the live site was given under awardsCountOnStatRow where it overruled DESIGN.md.
developerClientSiteAsSource.consequence: Five things on the page trace to those URLs rather than to DESIGN.md or a deck: the feasibility claim on truth card 2 and in FAQ 1, the $250 million stat bullet, two of the three service names, the budget bands, and the three named candidate records in the bracketed Tier 1 slots. Everything drawn from them is marked SOURCED in paper/developer-copy.md.
developerClientSiteAsSource.note: They are marketing pages, not verified records. Nothing there carries a date or a source of its own. Confirm both pages are current before this page takes paid traffic, and confirm the two figures that reach a live page: the $250 million total and the twenty named purchases.

developerFeasibilityClaim.problem: The question a developer asks before any other is whether the agency touches feasibility, planning or a DA. Nothing in the DESIGN.md claims register covered it, so the first draft of this page gated the question at Tier 3 and shipped without answering it, which left the page answering the wrong fear first.
developerFeasibilityClaim.decision: RESOLVED 21 Aug 2026 from the client own site. They publish "We typically run our own internal feasibility before presenting the site to a client" and "Our role in the development process is primarily locating a suitable development site and estimating sale values", and they list town planners among referral partners rather than services. So the page claims feasibility and sale value estimates, and hands planning to a referral. It appears on truth card 2 and as FAQ 1.
developerFeasibilityClaim.consequence: This is the sentence the page is built around, and it is the second half of the segment register: DESIGN.md asks this page to lead with site access and resale numbers, and "estimating sale values" is the resale number in the client own words.
developerFeasibilityClaim.openQuestion: The source says "typically" run our own internal feasibility. The card and the FAQ both say it is run, without the hedge, which is the normal reading of that word in marketing copy. Confirm feasibility is run on every site rather than most.
developerFeasibilityClaim.note: DA, zoning, yield modelling and highest-and-best-use are claimed NOWHERE on either client page, checked directly, and are claimed nowhere on this page either. The FAQ answer names four referral professions where the source names six, cut to avoid a triadic rhythm.

developerBudgetBands.problem: DESIGN.md section Segments puts this segment at "$2.5m upward": one number and an open top, where commercial had a closed $600k to $20m range and investor a closed $650k to $2m. The BRIEF asked for the ranges to be confirmed before build. They were not supplied.
developerBudgetBands.decision: FIVE BANDS DERIVED FROM THE CLIENT OWN PUBLISHED DEALS, 21 Aug 2026: under-2.5m, 2.5m-5m, 5m-10m, 10m-20m, 20m-plus. The client publishes twenty named site purchases and every one of the five bands is evidenced by at least one of them.
developerBudgetBands.status: DERIVED FROM PUBLISHED EVIDENCE, STRONGER THAN THE OTHER TWO PAGES
developerBudgetBands.consequence: This contradicts DESIGN.md at both ends and DESIGN.md is behind, NOT corrected here. The published deals run from $1.35m, which is below the stated $2.5m floor, to $57m at Kurraba Point, which is far above the $25m top band the first draft derived from DESIGN.md alone. Either the site is out of date or DESIGN.md is, and that is a client question rather than a build decision. The precedent is awardsCountOnStatRow.
developerBudgetBands.note: Unlike commercialBudgetBands and investorBudgetBands, these are not ASSUMED. Each band points at a real purchase. 20m-plus is byte-identical to the commercial page top band, which slightly reduces the fourteen-distinct-values sprawl recorded under investorBudgetBands as the input the HubSpot schema decision is waiting on.
developerBudgetBands.outstanding: Whether the DESIGN.md $2.5m floor or the published $1.35m deal is current. Changing these option values after launch breaks HubSpot routing the same way the segment strings do.

baseCssPromotion.decision: The site header, the site footer and the lead capture component (lead-card, chips, fields, inputs, form steps) moved from landing.css into base.css on 21 Aug 2026, when the first location page needed them. Moved, not copied.
baseCssPromotion.reason: The header and footer were byte identical across all three built paid pages, which is the evidence the split left the promotion waiting for. The capture component is contractual with assets/js/page.js and carries the settled chip selected state, so two copies would drift apart exactly where HubSpot routing depends on them.
baseCssPromotion.consequence: base.css now lands on every page in both families. Treat a change to it like a change to Figma Variables. The lead card hero sizing stayed in landing.css on a .hero .lead-card selector, because a fixed 460px width is hero composition, not component. Two conflicting mobile header rules from different rounds were collapsed to the winning one; behaviour is unchanged and npm run check verified every rendered check on all built pages after the move.
